items.question: Is JobLume free to use?
items.answer: JobLume is currently free, meeting basic resume creation needs. The open-source version's features will remain unchanged

items.question: Is my resume data secure?
items.answer: Yes, very secure. JobLume uses local storage, meaning all your data is stored on your own device with no cloud storage, ensuring complete privacy protection.

items.question: What export formats are supported?
items.answer: We currently support PDF export, PNG long image export, browser print, JSON config export, and Markdown export. PDF is best for formal applications and archiving, while PNG long image is useful for mobile previews, portfolio display, or image-upload workflows.

items.question: How can I sync across devices?
items.answer: We provide JSON configuration export, allowing you to save your resume settings in JSON format, accessible anytime, anywhere, on any device.

items.question: How customizable is it?
items.answer: We offer rich customization options, including colors, layouts, and more, allowing you to adjust your resume style according to personal preferences and industry requirements.

browser-compatibility.question: Which browser is recommended?
browser-compatibility.answer: We recommend using the latest version of Chrome or Edge for the best layout and export experience. Some outdated browsers may cause styling issues.

export-failure.question: What if export fails or style is broken?
export-failure.answer:
1. We recommend using Google Chrome (https://www.google.cn/intl/zh-CN/chrome/) for best compatibility.
2. If it still fails, try in 'Incognito Mode' to exclude extension interference.
3. Alternatively, click 'PDF (Backup)' in the export menu and select 'Save as PDF' in the print dialog.

export-methods.question: Which export format should I use?
export-methods.answer:
• PDF: Uses the backend service for high-precision rendering. Recommended for formal applications, printing, and archiving.

• PDF (Long Page): Renders the resume as an image in a custom-height, single-page PDF. Best for online preview and sharing; not recommended for printing, text selection, or ATS parsing.

• PNG (Long Image): Exports the resume as one tall image. Best for mobile preview, portfolios, and image-upload workflows.

• PDF (Backup): Uses the browser's print dialog to save a PDF. Use it when the primary export service is unavailable or when you need to adjust print margins manually.

• JSON Config: Exports a resume data backup for restoration or migration.

• Markdown: Exports plain text for use in other tools.

drag-and-drop.question: How do I drag and drop to reorder modules?
drag-and-drop.answer: In the 'Layout' settings of the left edit panel, hover your cursor over the 'Drag Handle' (usually represented by a six-dot icon) on the left side of the module card. Click and hold the left mouse button to drag the module up or down to reorder the sections of your entire resume.

profile.subtitle: Keep every experience in one place; pick what you need per resume

hints.title: Matching hints (optional)
hints.why: These never appear on the resume. They only feed the future job-matching analysis. Leaving all of them empty is fine.
hints.category.placeholder: e.g. Finance, Engineering, Operations — press Enter
hints.categoryNote: The first tag is the category. In general-resume ranking, too many entries from one category get down-weighted so the resume doesn't collapse into a single field.

basic.name: Name
basic.photoNote: Uploaded locally, auto-cropped to 3:4 and compressed into browser IndexedDB — it does not consume the localStorage quota.
basic.customFieldsNote: The toggle controls whether the field appears on the resume. Empty fields are hidden.
basic.jobTitleHint: The line right under your name in the resume header. Put your professional headline here, not the job you're applying for.
basic.statusHint: A contact-area field for your current job-seeking status, e.g. "Open to offers" or "Available immediately". Usually omitted on Western resumes.
basic.locationNote: Pick province and city; add a detailed address in a custom field below if needed.
basic.birthDateNote: Month precision only — that's all a resume needs.

skills.empty: No skill groups yet — add one to start
skills.newGroupPlaceholder: New group name, e.g. Frontend frameworks
skills.note: Renders as "Group name: content" on the resume. Skill names are extracted later by the AI matching step — no need to split them yourself.

selfEvaluation.placeholder: A few sentences on your strengths and positioning
selfEvaluation.note: This text appears verbatim in the resume's summary section and can be edited per resume after generation.

certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.empty: No certificates yet. Upload scans or photos — they'll be laid out side by side at the width you pick.
certificates.storageNote: Images live in IndexedDB (auto-compressed to 1200px max edge) and don't consume the localStorage quota. Full backups exclude these binaries — re-upload after switching devices.

generic.title: Generate General Resume
generic.description: Not tailored to any specific role — good for broad applications. The default selection is ranked by recency and category diversity; adjust freely.
generic.noEntities: Your career database is empty. Add a few experiences on the left, then come back.
generic.orderNote: Order: recency first, same-category entries down-weighted
generic.sameCategoryNote: Entry #{rank} in its category, ranking weight {score}

photo.cropHint: Drag to reposition, use the slider to zoom. The ratio is fixed at 3:4 (ID-photo standard).

save.failed: Save failed — browser storage may be full
save.autoNote: Changes persist as you type; switching sections won't lose anything.

targets.title: Job Targets
targets.subtitle: Paste a JD and let AI flag which experiences belong in this resume
targets.selectOrCreate: Pick a target on the left, or create one
targets.jdPlaceholder: Paste the full job posting here…
targets.jdNote: Paste the complete JD including requirements — the raw text goes straight to the model with no pre-parsing.
targets.warnShort: The JD looks short; analysis quality may suffer
targets.warnNoSection: This doesn't look like a complete job posting (no requirements/duties section found)
targets.warnNoNumbers: No concrete numbers found (years, headcount, percentages); results may be vague
targets.needApiKey: Configure an API key under AI Providers before using smart matching
targets.usedCache: Data unchanged; reusing the previous result. Use "Ignore cache and re-run" to force a fresh analysis.
targets.fallbackHint: You can still pick experiences manually — generation never depends on AI.
targets.corrections: Corrected {count} non-conforming items from the model

coverage.title: Skill coverage
coverage.missingNote: Missing items are reported only; the tool will not fabricate experience for you.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description: Export your career database, all resumes, and all job targets as a single JSON file. The three are linked in the data layer, so they must be backed up together to stay consistent.
backup.neverBackedUp: Never backed up. Clearing your browser cache wipes everything — export regularly.
backup.imageNote: Photos and certificates are embedded as Base64 and will be included, which makes the backup file fairly large. That's expected.
backup.importSuccess: Imported {resumes} resumes and {targets} targets ({skipped} duplicates skipped)

confirm.title: Confirm import
confirm.mergeHint: Merge: only non-duplicate items are added; existing data stays untouched. Good for combining two devices.
confirm.replaceHint: Replace: wipes all current data and writes the backup contents. This cannot be undone.
